# Trainset Elastic Energy Engine Utility

## Full tensor generation

Materials Project source runs now retain the complete symmetric 6x6 stiffness
tensor, rotate it from IEEE axes into the generated structure's Cartesian frame,
and sample 21 strain modes that resolve all 21 independent tensor entries. Non-orthogonal cells are included by
default. `--skip-not-orthogonal` remains an optional cell-angle filter.

For manual YAML, add `elastic.tensor_gpa` (six rows of six numbers in GPa) and
`elastic.tensor_frame: cell_cartesian`. The tensor frame must match the input XYZ
and the lattice constructed by ASE `cellpar_to_cell`: a along x, b in the xy
plane. The Voigt order is xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy, with engineering shear strains
2 epsilon_yz, 2 epsilon_xz, 2 epsilon_xy. Matrix entries explicitly include zeros;
the generator does not infer missing low-symmetry couplings. When present, this
matrix is authoritative; `cij_gpa` is only a readable nine-component summary.

Targets are second-order Taylor energies about a stress-free reference:
Delta E = V0/2 * eta.T C eta, with the existing kcal/mol conversion. For each
deformation path F(delta), eta is delta times the symmetric Cartesian tangent
at delta=0. Existing volume-conserving paths retain their quadratic energies;
finite-strain terms of third and higher order are not included. Normal modes
have unit normal strain; shear modes have engineering shear 2 delta. Normal
pairs use opposite signs, as in the original generator. Additional normal/shear
and shear/shear pairs use matching positive signs. All 21 modes are sampled even
when symmetry makes some coupling constants zero.

The bulk branch still uses the legacy third-order Birch-Murnaghan expression
and B0_prime=1.5 unless supplied otherwise. The CLI defaults to the Voigt modulus,
appropriate to uniform scaling; Reuss/VRH selections remain available but need
not agree with a uniform-strain tensor curvature. B0_prime is an assumed input,
not derivable from a second-order tensor. Strain grids round up to the next step,
as in the original energy generator, and every geometry generator uses
exactly the same grid. Zero targets retain the legacy 0.0001 offset.

Existing orthogonal YAML without `tensor_gpa` retains the nine-mode energy
targets. Both nine-constant and full-tensor inputs use corrected Cartesian
deformation, ReaxFF CRYSTX coordinate orientation, and matching energy/geometry
grids. Regenerate old GEO files to obtain these fixes; their coordinates and
endpoint coverage can differ from historical output. No tensor is invented
for a nine-constant input. Incomplete non-orthogonal YAML is still rejected
unless explicitly skipped; re-fetch it to recover the full tensor and its
orientation. Input XYZ coordinates must match the ASE `cellpar_to_cell` frame;
only the generated output coordinates are rotated into the ReaxFF frame.

MP tensors are relaxed-ion quantities (`elastic.response: relaxed_ion` in new
source YAML), while generated coordinates are affine starting structures.
Relax internal coordinates at fixed strained cell when fitting relaxed-ion
energies; fixed-coordinate targets require a compatible clamped-ion tensor.
The generator does not calculate internal relaxation, forces, anharmonicity,
or finite-pressure corrections. A non-positive tensor eigenvalue is reported
as instability; data are not silently projected onto a stable tensor. Negative
off-diagonal entries alone do not imply instability. The existing explicit
`--skip-negative-elastic-data` option filters any negative component, including
the extra couplings, rather than implementing a stability test.
